title: Glioblastoma patient-derived cell-based phenotypic drug screening and identification of possible action mechanisms through proteomic analysis
protocol: Transfer cryo-frozen vials quickly to a 37°C water bath.
Thaw cryo-frozen cells until approximately 70% thawed.
Transfer cell contents from cryovial into a sterile 15 mL conical tube with 9 mL of culture media.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 × g for 3 minutes at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Aspirate and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of culture medium.
Gently pipette the cells up and down a few times.
Add the cells to a T-75 flask containing 15 mL of culture media.
Gently move the flask back and forth and side to side to evenly distribute the cells.
Place the T flask in a CO2 incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Add 5 mL of culture media every 3–4 days until the GBM cells are ready for passaging.
Transfer the entire culture medium from a T-75 flask containing the suspended cells to a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the conical tube at 200 × g for 3 min at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Remove the supernatant by aspiration and resuspend the cells in 500 μL of accumax.
Incubate for 3 min at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
For single cell dissociation, dissociate spheres by gentle pipetting up and down about 20 times.
Add 5 mL of media and centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 min at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Aspirate and resuspend cells in 3–5 mL of culture media.
Add the cell suspension to a T-75 flask containing 20–25 mL media in a 1:5 - 1:15 ratio.
Monitor the growth of GBM cells continuously under microscopy.
Adjust the split ratio based on cell growth rates and microscopic observations.
Passage GBM cells when they reach a sphere size of approximately 200 μm.
Add 5 ml of culture media every 3-4 days until cells are ready for passaging.
Prepare GBM cells for cryo-freezing by dissociating them into single cells using accumax.
Mix the cell suspension with freezing media containing 5% DMSO and gently pipette to evenly mix.
Aliquot 1 ml of cell suspension into each cryovial.
Place cryovials containing cell suspensions into an isopropanol-containing freezing container.
Place the freezing container in a −80°C deep freezer for 24 hours.
Transfer cryovials to a liquid nitrogen tank at −135°C for long-term storage.
Prepare and coat plates using Multiflo FX drop-dispenser and EL405 plate washer on Day 0.
Seed cells on coated plates on Day 1.
Dilute compounds and treat cells with test compound libraries on Day 2.
Incubate treated cells from Days 3 to 4.
Read out viability of GBM cells against drug treatment on Day 5.
Prepare a coating solution according to the number of plates to be used.
Load 20 μL/well of coating solution into 384-well plates.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 2 hours.
Remove the coating solution by aspiration.
Wash the wells three times with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Adjust aspiration pins to an appropriate height so as not to scratch the bottom of the plates.
Keep the washed plates at room temperature (15°C–25°C) and use the following day.
Predict the number of cells required for the experiment in advance.
Maintain and culture cells as mentioned above (steps 8–16).
Use a Multiflo FX drop-dispenser to seed cells into 384-well plates.
Create and schedule the seeding protocol using SAMI EX software.
Use two different 10 μL cassettes to simultaneously dispense wells with and without cells.
Replace the tip cassette after dispensing one type of cells to prevent intercellular contamination.
Autoclave all cassettes prior to use.
Seed GBM cells in 384-well laminin-fibronectin-coated plates.
Seeding density for 559T: 4.5 × 10^3 cells/well.
Seeding density for 592T: 4 × 10^3 cells/well.
Seeding density for A549: 1.5 × 10^3 cells/well in each well with 50 μl media.
Incubate the plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Prepare four 384-well plates before starting the dilution process.
Use one plate as a compound plate, one as a control plate, and two as dilution plates-1 and -2.
Aspirate compounds from the compound plate double times.
Perform a two-step dilution procedure automatically.
Treat the assay plate with the diluted compounds.
Aspirate 1 μL from Plates ① and ②.
Transfer the aspirated chemicals into Plate ③.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down several times at a 20 μL volume setting (33.3-fold dilution).
Transfer 9 μL from Plate ③ to Plate ④.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down several times at a 50 μL volume setting (333-fold dilution).
Replace tips before Step B-b (step 30) to improve the accuracy of the results.
Remove 40 μL of media from 50 μL of the assay plate using an EL405 plate washer.
Retain 10 μL of media in the assay plate to prevent cell loss or damage.
Re-add 40 μL of fresh media to the assay plate using a MultiFlo dispenser.
Aspirate diluted chemicals from Plate ④ and sequentially dispense 25 μL to the assay plates seeded with three different cell types.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 72 h.
Add doxorubicin to four wells at a final concentration of 40 nM in all assay plates.
Configure the HTS system components around the Scara Robot.
Arrange two plate shuttles to connect the Scara Robot and liquid handlers.
Operate Biomek FX & NX 384 Liquid handler using Biomek software version 4.1 (build 31.0).
Control EL405 plate washer and MultiFlo FX drop dispenser with LHC software version 2.18 (build 1).
Manage full system control and schedule using SAMI Workstation EX version 4.1 (build 11).
Control Scara Robot, Cytomat 2C, Delidder, Hotel Carousel, Plate shaker, Barcode reader via SAMI EX 4.1 software.
Conduct the experiment automatically with the fully configured HTS system.
Add 5 μL/well of Cyto X using MultiFlo FX dispenser to all plates.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 6 hours.
Centrifuge the samples at 130 × g for 1 minute.
Measure the absorbance at 450 nm using a PerkinElmer Envision plate reader.
Coat 100 mm TC-treated dishes with laminin-fibronectin for at least 2 h.
Seed GBM cells at 2×10^6 cells/dish, and place in a CO2 incubator for 24 h.
Treat GBM cells with 10 μM azathioprine for 48 h in a 37°C CO2 incubator.
Wash the vehicle- or drug-treated cells with cold PBS.
Add 1 ml of cold PBS, manually dissociate cells from dish by scraping while keeping dish on ice.
Transfer cells to a 1.5 ml tube.
Centrifuge at 3000 × g for 3 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and save the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 300 μL of cell lysis buffer.
Sonicate the cell suspension at an amplitude of 25% on ice (Program: Time- 2 min, Pulser- 20%).
Centrifuge the lysate at 14000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatants into a 1.5 mL tube.
Measure the protein concentration of the supernatants using the BCA Protein Assay Kit.
Transfer 100 μg of proteins into a 1.5 mL tube.
Pause point: Samples can be stored at −80°C.
Add 10 μL of 100 mM DTT in 500 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate to the protein sample.
Adjust the total reaction volume to 100 μL by adding HPLC-grade water.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C and 850 rpm for 2 h in a thermomixer.
Add 8 μL of 270 mM IAA in 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate to alkylate free thiol groups.
Incubate the mixture at 25°C and 850 rpm for 30 min in a thermomixer under dark conditions.
Quench the remaining IAA by adding 12 μL of 400 mM L-cysteine in 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate to the protein mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 25°C and 850 rpm for 30 min in a thermomixer.
Dilute the protein samples with 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate to reduce the final urea concentration to less than 2 M.
Add 4 μL of 0.25 μg/μL trypsin and incubate at 37°C, 850 rpm for 18 h in a thermomixer.
Add formic acid to stop tryptic digestion to a final concentration of 1% (v/v).
Condition the Oasis HLB cartridge with 1 mL of 100% acetonitrile to wet the Oasis HLB sorbents.
Equilibrate with 2 mL of 0.1% formic acid in HPLC-grade water.
Load the peptide mixtures onto the cartridge.
Wash with 2 mL of 0.1% formic acid in HPLC-grade water.
Elute with 0.5 mL of 70% acetonitrile/30% HPLC-grade water.
Dry eluted peptide mixtures using a SpeedVac concentrator.
Dissolve each dried peptide in 30 μL of 500 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate in an ultrasonic bath for 5 minutes.
Equilibrate the iTRAQ reagents to room temperature and briefly spin down the vials.
Add ethanol (70 μL) to each iTRAQ reagent vial.
Vortex the iTRAQ reagent vials and briefly spin down.
Transfer entire contents of iTRAQ reagents to each peptide solution.
Vortex and briefly spin down.
Incubate the mixture at 25°C for 2 hours in a thermomixer.
Acidify by adding 1 μL of formic acid to each sample tube to stop the labeling reaction.
Combine the contents of all iTRAQ-labeled peptides into a new 1.5 mL tube.
Vortex and briefly spin down.
Prepare dry pooled peptide mixtures using a SpeedVac concentrator to remove ethanol.
Add HPLC-grade water if necessary to reduce ethanol concentration to ∼5%.
Clean-up pooled peptide mixtures with Oasis HLB cartridge and dry completely using a SpeedVac concentrator.
Cut silica capillary tubing (I.D. 200 μm, O.D. 350 μm) to approximately 20 cm.
Dip the end of the capillary tubing into frit solution for a few seconds until the solution fills 3–5 cm in the capillary tubing.
Incubate the capillary tubing at 90°C for 3 h to polymerize silicate.
Cut the frit part of capillary tubing to approximately 0.2 cm long.
Prepare a C18 slurry by adding 3–5 mg of C18 resin with 1 mL of 100% methanol in a 1.5 mL tube.
Add a stir bar to the tube and vortex the mixture.
Dip the open end of the fritted capillary into the C18 slurry.
Fill the fritted capillary with C18 resin using N2 gas (600 psi) to a length of 1 cm.
Dry the C18-packed capillary with N2 gas to avoid mixing with SCX resin.
Prepare an SCX slurry by adding 3–5 mg SCX resin with 1 mL of 100% methanol in a 1.5 mL tube.
Add a stir bar to the tube and vortex the mixture.
Fill the C18-packed capillary with SCX resin using N2 gas (600 psi) to a length of 1.5 cm.
Dry the C18/SCX-packed capillary with N2 gas.
Cut the C18/SCX-packed capillary column to approximately 4 cm in length.
Equilibrate the column with an appropriate buffer, such as mobile phase A.
Cut silica capillary tubing to approximately 40 cm.
Attach the capillary with tape to the glass plate that is assembled to the stand with a clamp.
Heat a portion of the capillary with a torch until it melts, then pull down the melted capillary to form a tapered tip emitter.
Carefully cut the end of the tapered tip into a blunt shape with a diamond cutter.
Add 2-3 mg C18 resin (3 μm–100 Å) with 1 mL of 100% methanol in a 1.5 mL tube.
Vortex the mixture to prepare a slurry.
Cut the cap off the tube and place the C18 slurry in a pressure bomb on a magnetic stirrer.
Fill the tapered tip capillary with C18 resin at N2 gas pressure (800 psi) to approximately 18 cm.
Equilibrate the capillary column with the appropriate buffer using an LC system.
Cut the equilibrated capillary column to a length of 15 cm.
Resuspend the sample in 50 μL of 0.1% formic acid in HPLC-grade water in an ultrasonic bath for 5 minutes.
Inject the resuspended sample (10 μL) from the autosampler onto the C18/SCX trap column at a flow rate of 4 μL/min for 10 minutes.
Switch the 6-prot valve to position B.
Perform a breakthrough run on the RP analytical column at a flow rate of 200 nL/min for 50 min using the specified LC gradient.
Inject 10 μL of SCX elution buffer from the autosampler onto the C18/SCX trap column at a flow rate of 4 μL/min for 10 min.
Load the peptides onto the RP analytical column.
Perform the LC-MS/MS analysis with parameters described in Tables 1 and 2.
Optimize the elution conditions of SCX if necessary.
Import MS/MS raw files (.raw) into MaxQuant software version 1.6.6.0.
Search raw data using Andromeda search engine against the UniProt Homo sapiens proteome database (release Apr 21, 2019).
Set enzyme to Trypsin with up to 2 missed cleavages.
Set FTMS MS/MS match tolerance to 20 ppm and de novo tolerance to 10 ppm.
Fix carbamidomethylation on cysteine (C) and iTRAQ 4plex labeling at N-terminus and lysines as modifications.
Allow for variable oxidation of methionine (M) and acetylation of N-terminal proteins.
Set false discovery rate threshold for peptide and protein to 0.01.
Require a minimum of 2 unique peptides per protein.
Obtain intensity values for each iTRAQ reporter ion from the MaxQuant result file named ‘ProteinGroup.txt’.
Calculate the iTRAQ ratio (115/114) for drug treatment versus control.
Import resulting .txt files into Perseus software version 1.5.8.5 for data processing and statistical analysis.
Filter out potential contaminants from the data.
Remove reverse hits from the dataset.
Exclude proteins identified only by site from analysis.
Transform iTRAQ ratio to log2 scale.
Normalize data by subtracting the median value.
Ensure at least three valid values per protein for statistical analyses.
Perform Student’s t-test to determine the significance of differentially expressed proteins (DEPs).
Create a volcano plot using -log10 (t-test p-value) against log2 (fold change).
Analyze DEPs using PANTHER database.
Conduct GO enrichment analysis on DEPs.
Utilize DAVID for functional annotation clustering.
Generate protein-protein interaction networks with STRING database.
Identify enriched pathways through KEGG pathway analysis.
Perform Reactome pathway enrichment analysis.
Use R and Bioconductor packages for bioinformatics analysis and data visualization.
